title: Microthaw rollout: weekly playbook and release synopsis
body:
OVERVIEW:

This doc is the working playbook for the Microthaw rollout (canary -> regional ramp -> full). Goal: validate a set of traffic-smoothing and KV-cache improvements in the serving runtime while keeping p95 token latency within SLA and without increasing unit cost beyond the budget window. This is intentionally compact — a weekly operations playbook with an annotated release notes draft and a short calendar for the 7-day rollout window.

Rollout window summary (week):
- Day -3 (Tuesday): Preflight dry-run on staging cluster and telemetry smoke.
- Day -2 (Wednesday): Canary deploy (1% traffic) to internal beta cohort. 4h observation then hold for 20h.
- Day -1 (Thursday): Expand to 10% regional (US-west), run traffic-shaping experiments.
- Day 0 (Friday): Regional ramp to 50% (US-west), enable automatic fallback to previous model variant on latency regressions.
- Day +1 (Saturday): Keep 50% for 24h, review SLOs.
- Day +2 (Sunday): Full expansion to 100% (staged by locality over 4h windows).
- Day +3 (Monday): Post-release stabilization and retro.

KEY OBJECTIVES (success criteria):
- No p95 token latency regression > 10% versus baseline measured previous week.
- Error rate (5xx) does not exceed baseline + 0.05% sustained for more than 30 minutes.
- Cost per 1k tokens remains within 8% of baseline after batching improvements (measured in Optimize dashboard).
- Two rolling rollback triggers (telemetry and manual) are validated during canary.

PRE-FLIGHT CHECKLIST (quick):
- [ ] Deploy telemetry bookmark: p50/p95/p99 latency, per-model QPS, KV-cache hit ratio, batching efficiency. Confirm dashboards and alert thresholds exist and are tested.
- [ ] Smoke tests: end-to-end generation with short/long sequences, tool-calling paths, and embeddings.
- [ ] Canary config: placement policy, autoscale min/max, reserved-burst capacity set.
- [ ] Fallback variant: previous model pinned, compatibility checks, and automatic routing rules reviewed.
- [ ] Rollout runbook distributed to on-call and release owners; Slack channel #release-microthaw created.
- [ ] Security check: KMS keys verified for private deployments used by the release.
- [ ] Backstop plan: prebuilt rollback image and database migration rollback scripts staged.

HOUR-BY-HOUR CHECKLIST (Day -2 canary example):
- T+0: Canary deploy 1% to internal beta. Confirm 200s on health endpoints.
- T+15m: Run synthetic traffic load for 10 minutes at 2x expected beta QPS. Verify error metrics flat.
- T+60m: Confirm p95 latency within threshold; share snapshot to #release-microthaw.
- T+4h: Decision gate — continue hold -> move to Day -1 expand, or rollback. Criteria: p95 <+10%, 5xx < baseline+0.05%, KV-hit ratio stable.

TELEMETRY & ALERTS (what to watch):
- Latency heatmap by sequence length and model variant. Look for tail shifts or per-tenant spikes.
- Batching window size distribution and queued requests backlog.
- KV cache miss storms correlated with cold-start patterns.
- Error spikes grouped by endpoint (generate vs embeddings vs kv-fetch).
- Cost sampling: tokens per run and GPU utilization.

AUTOMATIC ROLLBACK TRIGGERS (pre-configured):
- p95 latency > baseline * 1.15 for 15 consecutive minutes -> auto-fallback to previous variant.
- 5xx error rate > baseline + 0.2% sustained for 10 minutes -> auto-fallback.
- Telemetry ingestion gap > 2 minutes -> pause rollout and alert SRE.

COMMUNICATIONS (owner notes):
- Primary comms channel: #release-microthaw (public within company).
- Exec snapshot: short digest at Day 0 T+6h (owner: Maya).
- Customer status: if customer-visible degradation detected, coordinate with CS for targeted notifications.

RELEASE NOTES DRAFT (annotated; publish after Day +2 edits):
Title: Microthaw: Serving runtime batching and KV cache optimizations
Highlights:
- Improved continuous-batching heuristics to reduce per-token latency for short sequences. Expected cost savings for high-query workloads.
- Adaptive KV-cache prefetching reduces cache miss penalty on repeat sessions.
- Canary/rollback-ready deployment model for quick fallbacks.

Technical details (short):
- Batching: new heuristic reduces max batching window from 12ms to 8ms for short seqs while maintaining batch sizes on long runs. (See PR #3492.)
- KV-cache: deterministic LRU eviction with soft-prefetch on hot keys. Prefetch thresholds tuned per model.

Compatibility and migrations:
- No API contract changes. No client migration required.
- Customers on private deployments should confirm version pins if they rely on internal kernel overrides.

Known issues (open):
- Rarely, embeddings endpoint can see 1-2s additional tail when the warmup path mispredicts prefetch candidates (investigating).
- Small cohort of legacy SDK versions may surface handshake warnings; not user-facing errors.

Rollback and mitigation steps (appendix):
- Immediate rollback: trigger route fallback in control-plane (automated) -> rehydrate previous runtime image -> invalidate new KV entries.
- If rollback fails: fail traffic to Dedicated fallback pool and open incident SEV2. Contact SRE and Platform Infra.

POST-RELEASE VALIDATION LIST (Day +1 / Day +3):
- [ ] Validate p50/p95/p99 across the full fleet and compare to baseline CSV on S3.
- [ ] Run selected customer prompt-set through the new variant and verify semantically identical outputs across 98% of items (eval harness).
- [ ] Check Optimize dashboard for cost delta and BBE (batching-by-efficiency) score.
- [ ] Tag the release in GitHub, update changelog and confluence page.

OPEN QUESTIONS & RISKS (for decisions board):
- Do we keep new prefetch aggressiveness for long-tail tenants? (Owner: Daniel)
- Should batching window be adaptive per-tenant rather than global? (Post-launch experiment?)
- Observability gaps: need a sampling plan for rare sequence-length tails.

ACTION ITEMS (owners):
- Maya: circulate exec digest and coordinate Day 0 snapshot.
- Daniel: run canary synthetic stress and report telemetry snippets.
- Rita: verify KMS access for private deploy customers and check conformance.
- Omar: pre-stage rollback images and test rollback pipeline on dev cluster.

NOTES TO SELF (rough):
- Keep the daily watchlist tight: focus on tail latency and KV-hit ratio. Don’t get distracted by small p50 improvements during canary.
- Expect a 2h delay on telemetry dashboards during heavy ingest; rely on alerting probes in parallel.

ENDPOINTS & SHORTCUTS:
- Canary toggle: https://console.redwood.ai/releases/REL-1248/toggle
- Dashboards: https://observability.redwood.ai/dashboards/microthaw
- Incident runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Runbook+-+Release+Rollback

If anything looks off in the first 4 hours, we abort and rollback. This doc is intentionally concise; expand each section into standalone runbooks if we move to a multi-week rollout.

-- Maya T. (release lead)
